title: Every Card Now Explains Itself, In Two Languages | vitalii.no
description:
My son can't read yet, so his wall tasks are built wordless on purpose — just pictures and an anchor letter. But the parent-facing summary at the top of each zone still showed a blinking question mark with no instruction, and he had no way to know what a card was actually asking him to do without me standing right there.

Every card the task generator produces now sets an instruction field through a small helper that pairs a Bokmal sentence with its Ukrainian translation, naming the concrete letter, number, or action the exercise is testing — for example "Hvilken bokstav begynner alle tre pa?" alongside "Na yaku bukvu pochynayutsya vsi try?" for an anchor-letter task. The exercise itself stays wordless — he still can't read the instruction — but a parent or older sibling standing nearby can read it aloud in either language.

Every card he sees now covers letter-recognition, number, handwriting, and pairing tasks alike, each carrying its instruction in two languages instead of a wordless question mark.
